commands.name: IFCFileOperation
commands.description: Executes an IFC file operation: opens or merges an IFC file, or saves the project as an IFC file. A save can name the export translator to use, a merge the story the IFC file's first storey is placed on. With overwrite false a save refuses to replace an existing file.

method.description: The file operation method to use.

ifcFilePath.description: The target IFC file to use. The save method overwrites an existing file, unless overwrite is false.

overwrite.description: Optional, true by default. Only for the save method: false refuses to save when a file already exists at ifcFilePath, and writes nothing.

fileType.description: The type of the IFC file. The default is 'ifc'.

translatorName.description: Only for the save method: the name of the IFC export translator to save with, as GetIFCExportTranslators lists them. Without it the save runs with the translator Archicad would offer in its own Save dialog. Needs a fileType of ifc or ifczip (ifc or ifcxml on Archicad 25 and 26).

elementsToExport.description: Only for the save method, and only together with translatorName. The default is VisibleElementsOnAllStories.

storyIndex.description: Only for the merge method: the story the first storey of the IFC file is placed on, the IFC's other storeys follow on the stories above it. Without it Archicad uses the active story of the floor plan. The active story and the current window are restored after the merge. See GetStories for the valid story indices.

example.description: Saves the project as an IFC file with IFCFileOperation, using the first IFC export translator of the project. The file is written into a new temporary folder. The open and merge methods take the same ifcFilePath; open replaces the open project.
example.code:
"""Saves the project as an IFC file with IFCFileOperation, using the first IFC export translator of the project.

The file is written into a new temporary folder. The open and merge methods take the same ifcFilePath; open replaces
the open project.
"""
import os
import tempfile

import aclib

translators = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetIFCExportTranslators')['translators']
ifcFilePath = os.path.join (tempfile.mkdtemp (), 'Project.ifc')

parameters = {
    'method': 'save',
    'ifcFilePath': ifcFilePath,
    'fileType': 'ifc'
}
if translators:
    parameters['translatorName'] = translators[0]['name']
    parameters['elementsToExport'] = 'EntireProject'

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('IFCFileOperation', parameters))
print ('IFC file saved to', ifcFilePath)

commands.name: GetIFCExportTranslators
commands.description: Lists the IFC export translators of the project in the order of Archicad's translator list. preview marks the first one, which the Archicad API documents as the preview translator; no API identifies the preview translator otherwise, and in some projects the IFC Translators dialog shows another one as preview. Pass one of the names to IFCFileOperation as translatorName.

translators.description: The IFC export translators of the project, in the order of Archicad's translator list. The first one, which the Archicad API documents as the preview translator, has preview true.

example.description: Lists the IFC export translators of the project with GetIFCExportTranslators, in the order of Archicad's translator list (preview marks the first one).
example.code:
"""Lists the IFC export translators of the project with GetIFCExportTranslators, in the order of Archicad's translator list (preview marks the first one)."""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetIFCExportTranslators'))

commands.name: GetElementsByIFCIds
commands.description: Retrieves the elements by the given IFC identifiers. Accepts IFC GlobalIds in every Archicad version.

ifcIds.description: A list of IFC identifiers to get the corresponding elements for. Each one is either an IFC GlobalId (22 characters) or, before Archicad 28, the 36 character GUID form that GetIFCIdsOfElements returns there as ifcId.

example.description: Finds elements by their IFC identifiers with GetElementsByIFCIds. Needs at least one Wall: the IFC identifiers of the first walls are read with GetIFCIdsOfElements first.
example.code:
"""Finds elements by their IFC identifiers with GetElementsByIFCIds.

Needs at least one Wall: the IFC identifiers of the first walls are read with GetIFCIdsOfElements first.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:3]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

elementIFCIds = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetIFCIdsOfElements', {'elements': walls})['elementIFCIds']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByIFCIds', {
    'ifcIds': [ids['ifcId'] for ids in elementIFCIds if 'ifcId' in ids]
}))

commands.name: GetIFCIdsOfElements
commands.description: Retrieves the IFC identifiers of the given elements. Before Archicad 28 it also returns their IFC GlobalIds.

example.description: Gets the IFC identifiers of the first three walls with GetIFCIdsOfElements. Needs at least one Wall.
example.code:
"""Gets the IFC identifiers of the first three walls with GetIFCIdsOfElements.

Needs at least one Wall.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:3]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetIFCIdsOfElements', {'elements': walls}))

commands.name: GetIFCPropertiesOfElements
commands.description: Retrieves the IFC properties of the given elements.

example.description: Gets the IFC properties of the first wall with GetIFCPropertiesOfElements and prints them by property set. Needs at least one Wall.
example.code:
"""Gets the IFC properties of the first wall with GetIFCPropertiesOfElements and prints them by property set.

Needs at least one Wall.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:1]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')
elementId = walls[0]['elementId']

response = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetIFCPropertiesOfElements', {'elements': [{'elementId': elementId}]})
for ifcProperty in response['elementIFCProperties'][0].get ('ifcProperties', []):
    print (ifcProperty['propertySetName'], ifcProperty['name'], '=', ifcProperty['value'])

commands.name: GetIFCAttributesOfElements
commands.description: Retrieves the IFC attributes (Name, Description, ObjectType, Tag, PredefinedType, LongName, ...) of the given elements, subelements included: the name, the IFC value type and the value of each attribute. On Archicad 25, 26 and 27 storedOnly returns only the attributes stored on the elements.

storedOnly.description: Return only the attributes stored on the elements, not the ones Archicad would generate on IFC export. Used only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27. Default: false.

example.description: Gets the IFC attributes (Name, Description, ObjectType, Tag, ...) of the first three walls with GetIFCAttributesOfElements. Needs at least one Wall.
example.code:
"""Gets the IFC attributes (Name, Description, ObjectType, Tag, ...) of the first three walls with GetIFCAttributesOfElements.

Needs at least one Wall.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:3]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetIFCAttributesOfElements', {
    'elements': walls,
    'storedOnly': False
}))

commands.name: SetIFCAttributesOfElements
commands.description: Sets the values of IFC attributes (Name, Description, ObjectType, Tag, ...) of elements. The attribute must be one GetIFCAttributesOfElements returns for the element; its IFC value type is kept. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now.

elementIFCAttributeValues.description: The IFC attribute values to set.

example.description: Sets the IFC Description attribute of the first wall with SetIFCAttributesOfElements, reads it back and restores it. Needs at least one Wall. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27.

commands.name: SetIFCPropertiesOfElements
commands.description: Sets local IFC properties on elements by creating or modifying single value (IfcPropertySingleValue) properties in the given property sets. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now.

elementIFCPropertyValues.description: The IFC property values to set. Only single value (IfcPropertySingleValue) properties are supported.

example.description: Sets a local IFC property of the first wall with SetIFCPropertiesOfElements and reads it back. Needs at least one Wall. The property 'Tapir_Example / Note' is removed again at the end. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27.

commands.name: GetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements
commands.description: Retrieves the IFC classification references of the given elements, subelements included: identification, name, location, description and sort (from Archicad 29), the name of the IfcRelAssociatesClassification (from Archicad 28), the referenced classification (name, source, edition, edition date, description and location) and whether the reference comes from the preview translator or is stored locally. On Archicad 25, 26 and 27 the source is not given and storedOnly returns only the references stored on the elements.

storedOnly.description: Return only the classification references stored on the elements, not the ones Archicad would generate on IFC export. Used only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27. Default: false.

example.description: Gets the IFC classification references of the first three walls with GetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements. Needs at least one Wall.
example.code:
"""Gets the IFC classification references of the first three walls with GetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements.

Needs at least one Wall.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:3]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements', {
    'elements': walls,
    'storedOnly': False
}))

commands.name: SetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements
commands.description: Stores IFC classification references (identification, name, location and the referenced classification with its name, edition, edition date, description and location) on elements. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now.

elementIFCClassificationReferences.description: The IFC classification references to store on the elements.

example.description: Stores an IFC classification reference on the first wall with SetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements and reads it back. Needs at least one Wall. The reference is removed again at the end. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27.

commands.name: RemoveIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements
commands.description: Removes IFC classification references stored on elements, given by the name of their classification and optionally their identification; without identification every stored reference of that classification is removed. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now. With dryRun true nothing is removed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each element that has a matching stored reference gets wouldDelete.

elementIFCClassificationReferences.description: The IFC classification references to remove from the elements. Only references stored on the elements (the ones GetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements returns with storedOnly) can be removed.

executionResults.description: One result for each input item, in the order of the input. On a dry run an element that has a stored IFC classification reference of the given classification (and identification, when given) gets wouldDelete.

example.description: Removes an IFC classification reference from the first wall with RemoveIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements. Needs at least one Wall. The removed reference is stored by the script first. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27.

commands.name: RemoveIFCPropertiesOfElements
commands.description: Removes local IFC properties, given by property set and property name, from elements. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now. With dryRun true nothing is removed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each element that has the local IFC property gets wouldDelete.

elementIFCProperties.description: The local IFC properties to remove.

executionResults.description: One result for each input item, in the order of the input. On a dry run an element that has the local IFC property gets wouldDelete.

example.description: Removes a local IFC property from the first wall with RemoveIFCPropertiesOfElements. Needs at least one Wall. The removed property 'Tapir_Example / Note' is set by the script first. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27.

commands.name: GetIFCSpatialStructure
commands.description: Returns the IfcProject, IfcSite and IfcBuilding objects of the project's IFC model (hash value, IFC type and GlobalId), and for the given elements the index of the story they are assigned to in the IFC model. Available from Archicad 28.

elements.description: Elements to get the IFC story index of. Optional.

project.description: The IfcProject object. Left out when Archicad does not report it.

site.description: The IfcSite object. Left out when Archicad does not report it.

building.description: The IfcBuilding object. Left out when Archicad does not report it.

elements.description: The story of each given element in the IFC model, in the order of the input. Left out when no elements were given.

example.description: Gets the IfcProject, IfcSite and IfcBuilding of the project and the IFC story index of the first walls with GetIFCSpatialStructure. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
example.code:
"""Gets the IfcProject, IfcSite and IfcBuilding of the project and the IFC story index of the first walls with GetIFCSpatialStructure.

Requires Archicad 28 or later.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:3]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetIFCSpatialStructure', {'elements': walls}))

commands.name: GetIFCAssignments
commands.description: Returns the IFC assignments of the project: the root IFC groups, and for each object the objects assigned to it (children) and the objects it is assigned to (parents). Each object is given by its hash value, its element where it belongs to one, its IFC type and its GlobalId. Available from Archicad 28.

rootGroups.description: The IFC groups (e.g. IfcGroup, IfcZone, IfcSystem) that are not assigned to another group.

childObjects.description: Each IFC object that has objects assigned to it, with those objects.

parentObjects.description: Each IFC object that is assigned to other objects, with those objects.

example.description: Gets the IFC assignments of the project with GetIFCAssignments: the root IFC groups and the objects assigned to each other. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
example.code:
"""Gets the IFC assignments of the project with GetIFCAssignments: the root IFC groups and the objects assigned to each other.

Requires Archicad 28 or later.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetIFCAssignments'))

Guid.description: A Globally Unique Identifier (or Universally Unique Identifier) in its string representation as defined in RFC 4122.

SuccessfulExecutionResult.description: The result of a successful execution.

FailedExecutionResult.description: The result of a failed execution.

DryRun.description: If true, the command makes all the checks of a real run and resolves the same targets, with the same errors, but changes nothing in the project and creates no undo step. The response is that of a real run with "dryRun": true added, and says for each target what the real run would do. Default is false.

DryRunFlag.description: Present, and true, only in the response of a dry run (the dryRun input was true): nothing was changed in the project.

WouldDeleteExecutionResult.description: The result of a dry run for a target that passed every check: a real run would delete it.

DeletionExecutionResult.description: The result of a deletion for one target. On a dry run a target that passed every check gets wouldDelete instead of being deleted.

name.description: The name of the translator, as the IFC Translators dialog shows it.

preview.description: Whether this is the first item of Archicad's translator list, which the Archicad API documents as the preview translator (the one the IFC properties of elements are previewed with). No API identifies the preview translator otherwise, and in some projects the IFC Translators dialog shows another translator as the preview one.

ElementIFCProperty.description: The details of an IFC property value of an element.

value.description: The value of the property as a string. List and enumerated values are separated by semicolons.

valueType.description: The IFC type of the value, for example IfcLabel or IfcLengthMeasure. For a table value it is the type of its defined values. Left out when the property has no value to take the type from.

enumerationReference.description: For an enumerated value, the values of the enumeration it refers to (IfcPropertyEnumeration), each as a string. Available from Archicad 28; left out when the property has none.

IFCObject.description: An object of the IFC model of the project, as the IFC API of Archicad 28 and later identifies it.

hashValue.description: The hash value of the IFC object identifier (ObjectID::GenerateHashValue), for matching the objects of one response to each other. It is not stable between sessions; use elementId or globalId to identify an object.

elementId.description: The element the IFC object belongs to. Left out when Archicad reports no element for it.

ifcType.description: The IFC entity type of the object, for example IfcWall. Left out when Archicad does not report it.

globalId.description: The IFC GlobalId of the object. Left out when Archicad does not report it.

ElementIFCProperties.description: The IFC properties of an element.

ElementIFCAttribute.description: An IFC attribute of an element, for example Name, Description, ObjectType, Tag, PredefinedType or LongName.

name.description: The name of the IFC attribute.

valueType.description: The IFC type of the value, for example IfcLabel, IfcText or IfcIdentifier.

value.description: The value of the IFC attribute. Missing when the attribute has no value.

ElementIFCAttributes.description: The IFC attributes of an element.

ElementIFCAttributesOrErrors.description: A list of the IFC attributes of elements or errors.

ElementIFCType.description: The IFC type of an element.

ElementIFCIds.description: The IFC identifiers of an element.

ifcId.description: The IFC identifier of the element. From Archicad 28 it is the IFC GlobalId (22 characters); before Archicad 28 it is the same identifier in the 36 character GUID form, and ifcGlobalId gives its GlobalId.

externalIFCId.description: The external IFC identifier of the element, in the same form as ifcId.

ifcGlobalId.description: The IFC GlobalId (22 characters) of ifcId. Only returned before Archicad 28, where ifcId is in the GUID form; from Archicad 28 ifcId already is the GlobalId.

externalIFCGlobalId.description: The IFC GlobalId (22 characters) of externalIFCId, empty when the element has no external IFC identifier. Only returned before Archicad 28.

ElementIFCPropertiesOrErrors.description: A list of the IFC properties of elements or errors.

ElementIFCTypesOrErrors.description: A list of the IFC types of elements or errors.

ElementIFCIdsOrErrors.description: A list of the IFC identifiers of elements or errors.

ElementIFCClassificationReference.description: An IFC classification reference (IfcClassificationReference) of an element. The text fields are missing when the reference has no value for them.

identification.description: The identification of the classification reference, for example a classification code.

name.description: The name of the classification reference.

location.description: The location of the classification reference, for example a URL.

description.description: The description of the classification reference. Given from Archicad 29.

sort.description: The sort key of the classification reference (its Sort attribute). Given from Archicad 29, missing when it has no value.

relAssociatesClassificationName.description: The name of the IfcRelAssociatesClassification relationship that links the reference to the element. Given from Archicad 28, missing when it is empty.

referencedSource.description: The classification (IfcClassification) the reference belongs to.

source.description: The source of the classification. Missing when it has no value.

edition.description: The edition of the classification. Missing when it has no value.

editionDate.description: The edition date of the classification. Missing when it has no value.

description.description: The description of the classification. Missing when it has no value.

location.description: The location of the classification, for example a URL. Missing when it has no value.

source.description: Where the reference comes from: preview (mapped by the preview IFC export translator) or local (stored on the element). Missing in Archicad 25, 26 and 27, where the storedOnly input chooses between the stored references and all of them.

ElementIFCClassificationReferences.description: The IFC classification references of an element.

ElementIFCClassificationReferencesOrErro.description: Element IFC classification references or error.
A list of the IFC classification references of elements or errors.

ElementsByIFCIds.description: A list of elements identified by their IFC identifiers or errors.

elements.description: A list of element identifiers having the given IFC identifier. If the given IFC identifier is an external identifier, the list can contain multiple elements as the IFC can be placed multiple times.

propertySetName.description: The name of the property set, for example Pset_DoorCommon. Custom property set names are also accepted.

propertyName.description: The name of the property, for example FireRating.

type.description: The IFC type of the value, for example IfcLabel, IfcText, IfcIdentifier, IfcBoolean, IfcLogical, IfcInteger, IfcReal or a measure type like IfcThermalTransmittanceMeasure. A type Archicad does not know is rejected.

value.description: The new value of the property. Provide a boolean for IfcBoolean and IfcLogical (IfcLogical also accepts the string Unknown), a number for the numeric types and a string for every other type.

identification.description: The identification of the classification reference, for example a classification code. Default: empty.

name.description: The name of the classification reference. Default: empty.

location.description: The location of the classification reference, for example a URL. Default: empty.

referencedSource.description: The classification (IfcClassification) the reference belongs to.

edition.description: The edition of the classification. Default: empty.

editionDate.description: The edition date of the classification. Default: empty.

description.description: The description of the classification. Default: empty.

location.description: The location of the classification, for example a URL. Default: empty.

referencedSource.description: The classification (IfcClassification) the reference belongs to.

identification.description: The identification of the classification reference to remove. When it is not given, every stored reference of the classification is removed from the element.

storyIndex.description: The index of the story the element is assigned to in the IFC model.

IFCPropertyType.description: The kind of the IFC property.

IFCPropertySource.description: Where the property comes from: preview for the properties mapped by the preview IFC export translator, local for the IFC properties stored in the element. Available from Archicad 28.

propertySetName.description: The name of the property set, for example Pset_DoorCommon.

propertyName.description: The name of the property, for example FireRating.

name.description: The name of the IFC attribute, for example Name, Description, ObjectType or Tag. It must be one of the attributes GetIFCAttributesOfElements returns for the element.

value.description: The new value of the IFC attribute.
